In a deployment with multiple instances, the AccessMatrix application servers are deployed with a Common Login Page (CLP), SSO Portal, and Self-Service Portal running together. A load balancer is needed in front of the CLP and USO instances to distribute the workload among the instances, ensuring that USO will only communicate with the AccessMatrix Server in the same instance. query: How do you activate a profile in USO applications and what role do user-defined actions play in this process?
ground_truth: To activate a profile in USO applications, you need to right-click on the desired profile and select the Set Active option. If the activation is successful, a message saying 'USO server/PSE updated successfully.' will be displayed on the USO Client's status bar, and the profile will be highlighted. User-defined actions allow administrators to define custom actions to cater to different screen matching behaviors, which can be crucial in managing and automating tasks related to profile activation and other processes within USO applications.
